name: Hannah's Lumen day as several chats, switched constantly (TWIN hannah2, 31 turns, v0.9.294): a Stripe webhook that drops events, a Safari thumbnail bug reported mid-morning and parked, a Studio profile section on the settings page, the deploy preview explained for a coworker, a Postgres full-text search index with one abandoned idea, the morning bug picked up again in the afternoon, the end-of-day questions — one growing map. (Topics only — never an outcome.)

rounds.user: Let's debug the Stripe billing webhook. Events seem to get dropped when two arrive within a second. First inspect the handler and help me reproduce it with the Stripe CLI.
rounds.assistant: I found the webhook handler and a likely race around the event-processing check. Let's first run two fixture events back-to-back with the Stripe CLI and capture the request logs before changing anything.

rounds.user: Run the back-to-back Stripe CLI reproduction and show me the logs for both events, especially where the processing check races.
rounds.assistant: Both events reached the handler, but each read the event as unprocessed before either write completed. One then overwrote the shared processing state, so the second event never completed. The logs confirm a check-then-write race.

rounds.user: Add idempotency keyed by the Stripe event ID. Store processed event IDs in Postgres and make the claim atomic so two events arriving together can't race.
rounds.assistant: I added a processed_stripe_events table keyed by event_id and changed the handler to atomically claim each event before processing. Duplicate deliveries now return success without running the handler twice.

rounds.user: Write a concurrency test that sends two different Stripe events at the same time and proves both are processed exactly once. Also add a duplicate-delivery test for the same event ID.
rounds.assistant: I added both tests: concurrent distinct events are each processed once, and duplicate deliveries of one event ID return success without repeating side effects. Both tests pass.

rounds.user: Now handle invoice.payment_failed. Make sure we record the failed payment, update the subscription state safely, and don't send duplicate customer notifications on webhook retries. Add the relevant tests.
rounds.assistant: I added the invoice.payment_failed path: it records the failure, updates the subscription to past_due in the same transaction, and gates notification delivery on the claimed Stripe event. Tests cover the state change and prove a retried event does not send a second notification.

rounds.user: Run the full webhook test suite now, including the new concurrency and payment-failed cases. Check that a processing failure rolls back cleanly so Stripe can retry the event instead of it staying permanently claimed.
rounds.assistant: The full webhook suite passes. I found that failed processing could leave the event claimed, so I moved the claim and side effects into one transaction; failures now roll back the claim and a Stripe retry can process the event normally. I added a regression test and it passes.

rounds.user: Before we wrap the webhook work, exercise the rollback-and-retry path with a realistic transient failure: fail the first processing attempt, retry the same Stripe event ID, and verify it succeeds exactly once with no duplicate side effects.
rounds.assistant: I added an integration test that injects a transient failure on the first attempt, then retries the same event ID. The claim rolls back, the retry succeeds, and all database updates and notifications occur exactly once. The webhook suite remains green.

rounds.user: Slack interruption: a customer says gallery thumbnails are blank in Safari. Please inspect the thumbnail rendering and image formats, reproduce the likely Safari-specific failure, and tell me what you find. Don't fix it yet — I need to park a clear finding and get back to the webhook.
rounds.assistant: I traced the blank thumbnails to galleries that only provide a WebP source. In the affected Safari versions, decoding fails and there is no JPEG/PNG fallback, so the image renders blank. I haven't changed the code; the fix should add a fallback source in the thumbnail picture markup.

rounds.user: Add a short note capturing the Safari finding: WebP-only thumbnails can render blank because there’s no JPEG/PNG fallback. Include the likely fix, but don’t change any code yet—we’re parking this and going back to the webhook.
rounds.assistant: I added a concise note documenting the WebP-only failure, affected Safari behavior, and the proposed picture-source fallback. No code was changed; the Safari thumbnail issue is parked for later.

rounds.user: Good. Add a concise changelog line for the Stripe webhook fix covering atomic event-ID idempotency, safe retries, and the payment-failed handling. Then show me the final diff summary for the webhook work.
rounds.assistant: I added the changelog entry and reviewed the final webhook diff. It now includes the processed-event table, atomic claims and rollback-safe retries, `invoice.payment_failed` handling, duplicate-notification protection, and the concurrency and retry regression tests.

rounds.user: Next, build a new Studio profile section on the Settings page. First inspect the existing settings patterns and sketch the form fields and component structure so it fits the app.
rounds.assistant: I inspected the existing Settings page and its form conventions. I’ll add a Studio profile section using the shared field and card components, with studio name, bio, website, and contact email fields, then wire validation and saving in the next steps.

rounds.user: Implement the Studio profile form UI now using those existing settings patterns and shared components. Add the studio name, bio, website, and contact email fields, but keep saving separate for the next step.
rounds.assistant: I added the Studio profile card and form fields using the existing Settings components and layout conventions. The fields are wired to local form state, but no save request has been added yet.

rounds.user: Add validation for the Studio profile form: require a non-empty studio name, validate the website URL and contact email, and show inline errors using the existing settings form patterns. Don't wire up saving yet.
rounds.assistant: I added client-side validation for the required studio name, website URL, and contact email, with inline errors matching the existing Settings forms. Saving is still unchanged and ready to wire next.

rounds.user: Wire up saving now. Add the Studio profile save endpoint, persist the validated fields, return useful field-level errors, and connect the form submit using the existing Settings patterns.
rounds.assistant: I added the Studio profile update endpoint and connected the form submission. Valid values persist successfully, server validation errors map back to the relevant fields, and the form follows the existing Settings save and error-state patterns.

rounds.user: Add an optimistic update for the Studio profile save. Update the visible profile immediately, restore the previous values if the request fails, and keep the inline server errors working.
rounds.assistant: I added the optimistic update: submitted profile values appear immediately, successful saves settle normally, and failed requests restore the previous profile while preserving field-level server errors.

rounds.user: Do an accessibility pass on the Studio profile form now. Check every field’s label and error association, keyboard focus order, focus behavior after a failed submit, and save-status announcements. Fix any issues you find.
rounds.assistant: I completed the accessibility pass. Each field now has an explicit label and associated error description, keyboard order follows the visual layout, failed submission focuses the first invalid field, and save success or failure is announced through an aria-live status region.

rounds.user: Add tests for the Studio profile section now: cover valid saves, field-level validation errors, optimistic rollback on failure, and the failed-submit focus behavior. Run the relevant Settings tests and fix anything that breaks.
rounds.assistant: I added Studio profile tests covering successful persistence, field-level validation, optimistic rollback, and focus moving to the first invalid field. The relevant Settings test suite passes.

rounds.user: I’m back and the main Studio profile work is green. Before we call it finished, check the empty-name edge case carefully: whitespace-only studio names, clearing an existing name, and any difference between client and server validation. Add or fix tests for whatever you find.
rounds.assistant: I found that the client rejected whitespace-only names, but the server accepted them after a direct request. I normalized the value before validation on both paths, reject cleared or whitespace-only names consistently, and added tests covering both cases. The Settings tests pass.

rounds.user: Now check the database schema for the Studio profile fields. Add the migration needed to persist studio name, bio, website, and contact email, update the model or query layer, and run the migration and relevant Settings tests.
rounds.assistant: I added the Studio profile columns and updated the profile query layer to read and write them. The migration applies cleanly, and the Settings and Studio profile tests pass.

rounds.user: Quick interruption: a coworker asked how our deploy previews work. Inspect the current preview-deploy setup and give me a concise explanation I can send them, including what triggers a preview, where the URL appears, and whether migrations run.
rounds.assistant: Deploy previews are created for each pull request after CI passes. The hosting integration posts the preview URL on the PR and updates it on subsequent pushes. The preview uses an isolated environment, and database migrations do not run automatically; schema-dependent changes need the documented preview-database workflow.

rounds.user: Great—add that concise deploy-preview explanation to the README so the next person can find it. Include the PR trigger, where the preview URL appears, and the fact that migrations need the separate preview-database workflow.
rounds.assistant: I added a concise Deploy previews section to the README covering the PR/CI trigger, the preview URL posted on the pull request, updates after new pushes, and the separate workflow required for database migrations.

rounds.user: Now let’s improve photo search. Inspect the current search query and schema, then propose how to search across title, tags, and caption with Postgres full-text search. Don’t implement it yet—show me the smallest sensible plan first.
rounds.assistant: I inspected the current search path: it uses a case-insensitive title match and has no search index. The smallest plan is to add a weighted `tsvector` over title, tags, and caption, index it with GIN, update the query to use `websearch_to_tsquery`, and add a backfill plus ranking tests before switching the endpoint.

rounds.user: Implement the weighted Postgres full-text search vector over title, tags, and caption now, with title weighted highest, then tags, then caption. Add the GIN index and migration, but don’t switch the search endpoint yet.
rounds.assistant: I added a generated weighted `tsvector` with title as weight A, tags as B, and caption as C, plus a GIN index and migration. The migration applies cleanly; the existing search endpoint is unchanged for now.

rounds.user: Add the backfill for the new photo search vector now. Make it safe to run on existing production rows, batch the work so it doesn’t hold one huge transaction, and add a dry-run or progress output so we can see what it will touch. Run it against the test database, but don’t switch the search endpoint yet.
rounds.assistant: I added a batched, resumable backfill for existing photos with dry-run and progress output. It avoids a single long transaction, completed successfully against the test database, and the search endpoint still uses the existing title-only query.

rounds.user: Switch the photo search endpoint from the title-only match to the new full-text query using `websearch_to_tsquery`. Rank title matches highest, then tags, then caption, keep the existing pagination behavior, and run the relevant search tests.
rounds.assistant: I switched the endpoint to the weighted full-text query with `websearch_to_tsquery` and `ts_rank`, preserving the existing pagination. Title matches rank above tag and caption matches, and the relevant search tests pass.

rounds.user: Before we lock this in, try a trigram index as an alternative for fuzzy and partial matches. Compare its query behavior and ranking with the full-text approach on our search fixtures, and tell me whether it’s actually worth keeping.
rounds.assistant: I added a temporary trigram-index variant and compared it with the full-text query. It helps with misspellings and partial strings, but produces noisier rankings for our title, tag, and caption fixtures and adds another index to maintain. I don’t recommend keeping it; the weighted full-text approach is the better fit unless fuzzy search becomes a separate requirement.

rounds.user: Agreed—drop the trigram approach. Remove the temporary trigram index and query variant, keep the weighted full-text implementation, and add a short code comment or decision note that fuzzy search is deferred as a separate future requirement. Then run the search tests again.
rounds.assistant: I removed the temporary trigram index and query variant, kept the weighted full-text implementation, and documented that fuzzy matching is deferred to a separate future requirement. The search tests pass.

rounds.user: Do one final search pass before we move on: add or verify tests proving matches work independently through title, tags, and caption, that title ranks above tags and caption, and that pagination stays stable. Run the full relevant search suite and tell me if anything remains open.
rounds.assistant: I added coverage for title-only, tag-only, and caption-only matches, verified the expected title > tags > caption ranking, and confirmed stable pagination across ranked results. The full search suite passes, and there are no remaining implementation tasks for this search change.

rounds.user: Let’s pick up the parked Safari thumbnail bug. Update the gallery thumbnail markup to provide a JPEG or PNG fallback for the WebP source using the existing image pipeline, without changing the current sizing or lazy-loading behavior. Add a focused test for the generated picture sources.
rounds.assistant: I added a JPEG fallback after the WebP source in the gallery thumbnail picture markup, preserving the existing dimensions and lazy-loading behavior. I also added a focused test verifying the source order and fallback URL; the relevant gallery tests pass.

rounds.user: Run the focused gallery thumbnail test in WebKit, then check the rendered picture markup against the Safari versions affected by the blank-thumbnail issue. Confirm the fallback actually loads when WebP is unavailable and that sizing and lazy loading still behave correctly.
rounds.assistant: The focused test passes in WebKit. I also verified the rendered picture behavior for the affected Safari path: when WebP is unavailable, the JPEG fallback loads correctly, while the existing dimensions and lazy-loading attributes remain unchanged.

rounds.user: Run the full gallery test suite and do a final regression check for Chrome and Firefox as well as Safari. If everything is green, add a concise changelog line for the thumbnail fallback and tell me whether anything remains open on this bug.
rounds.assistant: The full gallery suite passes, and the thumbnail still renders correctly in Chrome, Firefox, and Safari with sizing and lazy loading unchanged. I added a changelog line for the JPEG fallback. Nothing remains open on the Safari thumbnail bug.
